sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and router setup
sections.what: Brings in the router, list type, request checking, errors, the database session, the comparator model and the normalization service.
sections.why: Likely reason: the two endpoints below need these tools.
sections.watch_out: The research model is imported inside one function with a different path style, which may fail if the app runs from another folder.

sections.name: NormalizeRequest
sections.title: Normalize request shape
sections.what: Describes the normalize request: project ID, base quarter defaulting to 2024-Q2, base currency defaulting to USD, and optional comparator IDs.
sections.why: Likely reason: sets a common reference date and currency.
sections.watch_out: Defaults are fixed, so a caller who omits them silently gets 2024-Q2 and USD.

sections.name: NormalizedComparator
sections.title: One normalized result shape
sections.what: Describes one normalized result: comparable ID, normalized cost per MW and the factors used.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the caller see how each figure was adjusted.
sections.watch_out: The factors are untyped, so the caller must know their keys.

sections.name: NormalizeResponse
sections.title: Normalize reply shape
sections.what: Describes the reply: a count and the list of normalized results.
sections.why: Likely reason: a standard reply wrapper.
sections.watch_out: The count is the number processed, which is the same as the list length.

sections.name: ConflictDetectionRequest
sections.title: Conflict request shape
sections.what: Describes a conflict request with a project ID and the field name to check.
sections.why: Likely reason: conflicts are checked one field at a time.
sections.watch_out: The field name is free text, so a misspelled field returns no data rather than an error.

sections.name: ConflictDetectionResponse
sections.title: Conflict reply shape
sections.what: Describes the conflict reply with source count, median, spread, conflict list, recommendation and confidence label.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives enough to judge whether sources agree.
sections.watch_out: Conflicts are untyped dictionaries, so the reply does not check their contents.

sections.name: normalize_comparators
sections.title: Normalize comparables endpoint
sections.what: Loads the project's comparables, optionally narrows them to chosen IDs, runs each through the normalization service and returns each result.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the adjustment logic in the service and this route as a thin wrapper.
sections.watch_out: A comparable with no normalized total is reported as zero per MW, which looks like a real value.

sections.name: detect_conflicts
sections.title: Source conflict check endpoint
sections.what: Gathers extracted values for one field from the project's sources and asks the service to flag values far from the median and suggest an action.
sections.why: Likely reason: a sanity check on sourced numbers before they are used.
sections.watch_out: The service result is passed straight into the reply, so any key the reply does not expect makes the request fail.

summary: Exposes endpoints that adjust comparable project costs to a common basis and flag conflicting values from different sources.
purpose: Lets a caller normalize selected comparables and check whether a field's sources agree.
why: Likely reason: comparable costs must share the same date, currency and location before they can be compared, and conflicting sources must be spotted.
how: 1) The normalize endpoint sets the base quarter and currency, selects the project's comparables, runs each through the normalization service and returns the results. 2) The conflicts endpoint gathers values for one field from the project's sources and asks the service to flag outliers and recommend an action.
inputs: Project ID, base quarter, base currency and optional comparator IDs. Or a project ID and a field name.
outputs: A count and each comparable's normalized cost per MW with its factors. Or a conflict summary with median, spread, conflicts, recommendation and confidence label.
risks: The service logic is not in this packet, so the numbers cannot be verified here. A missing total becomes zero without warning. A missing factor key causes an error.
debug: If normalized values show zero, check what the service returns for that comparable. If conflicts come back empty, check that the project has extracts for that field.
